title: Thanksgiving Giving Sweeps Across Webb County: 5,000 Meals, Turkeys and Helping Hands
excerpt: Across Webb County this week, the Thanksgiving table is getting bigger — not because of one big event, but because neighbors, churches, schools and whole towns
content:
Across Webb County this week, the Thanksgiving table is getting bigger — not because of one big event, but because neighbors, churches, schools and whole towns each decided to feed somebody else.

In Laredo, Laredo First Assembly’s annual “Turkeys on the Table” outreach set out to deliver complete Thanksgiving meals to 5,000 people across the city on Nov. 23. Each meal bag carries a turkey, traditional sides and bread, and church volunteers spend the afternoon hand-delivering the bags to families in need. The church served 4,000 people through the same outreach in 2024, then raised its goal to 5,000 for this year, gathering donations of turkeys, stuffing, mashed potatoes, canned vegetables, gravy and bread at its campus at 6103 McPherson Road.

In El Cenizo, the giving took over the streets on Nov. 23. Mayor Carina Hernandez joined volunteers from South Texas Familia Unida, Loyalty Traditions Car Club, Texas Strong and the Twisted Toyz Laredo motorcycle club for a community Thanksgiving food distribution, handing out packaged turkeys and meal kits to families — with a volunteer in a turkey mascot costume working the crowd. Photos from the day show coolers and trays of food being unloaded from trucks and SUVs, and children, parents and seniors posing with the mascot while holding their donations.

And at Laredo ISD, the district held its first annual Westside Turkey Giveaway on Nov. 16 at Leon Daiches Elementary and Santa Maria Elementary, where school staff, trustees Rodolfo “Rudy” Morales III and Juan Ramirez Jr., and Superintendent Guillermo Pro handed out turkeys and bags of food to local families.

Three different efforts, three different corners of the county — and the same idea underneath them: nobody in Webb County should go without a Thanksgiving meal if their neighbors can help it.

Sources: Laredo First Assembly; City of El Cenizo / Mayor Carina Hernandez; Laredo Independent School District.
